concepts.name: Vision Encoder
concepts.summary: A model that maps an image to a representation: image -> encoder -> patch embeddings (n_patches, d) and often one global vector. Almost always a ViT (patchify the image into a grid, then run a transformer over the patches). The crucial fact: architecture is shared across encoders and is NOT what distinguishes them -- the training objective is. Swapping encoders in a real system is mostly a projector/dimension change.

concepts.name: Training Objective (Encoder Oath)
concepts.summary: The training signal that shapes an encoder's features -- the 'oath' it swears at training time -- and the true axis that differentiates vision encoders. Four families: match image to caption (CLIP/SigLIP, text-supervised -> language-aligned semantics); match two crops of the same image (DINO/DINOv2, self-supervised -> visual structure); reconstruct masked patches (MAE); predict a label (supervised ViT). Trained WITH text gives semantic, nameable features; trained WITHOUT text gives spatially precise, structural features with no language grounding.
